List the input arguments a TreePPL model expects

Source: R/data.R
tp_expected_input.Rd

Scans a .tppl file, finds its model function signature and reports the name of every input argument together with the R object you should supply for it. The result is printed to the console and also returned, invisibly, so it can be stored and reused (for example to check a data list before writing it to JSON).

Usage

tp_expected_input(tppl)

Arguments

tppl

Path to a .tppl model file.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class tpEdata with elements:

  • model_file: the path given in tppl.

  • model_name: the model's name, i.e. the file name without .tppl ("qt" for qt.tppl).

  • model_function: the name of the model function inside the file, which can differ from model_name ("qtbirds" in qt.tppl).

  • expect_args: character vector of argument names, in signature order.

  • expect_types: character vector of the TreePPL type of each argument.

  • expect_class: character vector of the matching R object.

Models without arguments return zero-length vectors.

Details

TreePPL types are translated to R objects as follows:

TreePPL typeR object
Realnumeric
Intinteger
Boollogical
Stringcharacter
Real[], Int[], ...numeric vector, ...
Real[][], Int[][], ...numeric matrix, ...
Matrix[Real]matrix
any recursive tree typephylo
anything else (e.g. record types)the TreePPL type

A type counts as a tree when it is ClockTree (TreePPL's built-in tree), an alias of a tree type, or a type defined in the model file (or in a file it imports with a relative path) whose fields refer to the type itself, e.g. Node {left: Tree, right: Tree, age: Real}.

See also

print.tpEdata() for the console output.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tp_expected_input(tppl = "models/diversification/clads2.tppl")

k <- tp_expected_input(tppl = "models/diversification/clads2.tppl")
k$expect_args
#> [1] "tree" "rho"
} # }
